result.summary: This PR makes PeerManagerImpl::m_tx_for_private_broadcast an std::optional so it is only constructed when -privatebroadcast=1 is set, rather than always existing. It is a follow-up to #29415, requested during that PR's review, and touches only src/net_processing.cpp related logic and guards around the optional's access.
result.problem: Currently the private-broadcast transaction queue exists unconditionally even for nodes that never use private broadcast, which is unnecessary state for the common case. Reviewers in #29415 asked for this to be made conditional to avoid needless resource use in the default configuration.

open_concerns: mzumsande: whether making the field optional makes sense at all depends on private broadcast's future direction, since other PRs (#35252) may push private broadcast into core node functionality; author has no resolution.
l0rinc: initialization boundary between constructor option and lazy InitiateTxBroadcastPrivate() call, largely addressed by moving init to the constructor.
Ongoing uncertainty about whether unreachable-state handling in guarded methods should use LogWarning, Assume(), or something else; unresolved as of last activity.
optout21 and polespinasa asked whether IsPrivateBroadcastConn()==true with the optional unset is actually reachable; treated as defensive-only, not fully settled.
resolved_concerns: l0rinc's initialization-order concern was addressed by moving construction into PeerManagerImpl::PeerManagerImpl().
Style nits about has_value() vs operator bool(): author explained rationale, not blocking.
A silent merge conflict causing CI failure was fixed by the author (added guards to new methods).

No external users or downstream consumers are cited as needing this change; it originates purely from a review request in #29415.
result.card: This PR makes PeerManagerImpl::m_tx_for_private_broadcast an std::optional so the private-broadcast transaction queue is only constructed when -privatebroadcast=1 is enabled, following up on a review request from #29415. It is a narrow internal cleanup within the opt-in private-broadcast subsystem with no stated user-facing benefit, bug fix, or measured performance gain (one reviewer notes the optional still reserves inline storage regardless). A maintainer, mzumsande, questions whether the premise even holds given other in-flight PRs (#35252) that could push private broadcast into core functionality, and the author agrees he has no answer. Maintainer fanquake moved the PR to draft, citing both the need for a rebase and unresolved decisions on private broadcast's overall direction, so review right now would likely be wasted. Several contributors gave Concept/Approach ACKs and most implementation nits were resolved, but the core direction question remains open.
